title: Four-Dimensional SCFT Data and Duality Frontier

items.title: Four-Dimensional SCFT and Protected Observable Data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored definition; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The selected classical model is the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills model with spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and global gauge group $G=SU(2)$ rather than $SO(3)$. Its field data are one $SU(2)$ connection, six real adjoint scalars, and four adjoint Weyl fermions, with the coupling and action normalization fixed by the selected model data. The gauge coupling $g>0$ is dimensionless in four dimensions. The model's sixteen-supercharge invariance is adopted as part of that classical model; this definition does not add a proof of invariance, a quantum measure, or a continuum construction.

A four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal field theory (SCFT) is, by definition here, a unitary positive-energy quantum field theory whose local-operator state space carries the four-dimensional conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$ together with its $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal extension. The real Lie superalgebra for the selected maximally supersymmetric case is $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$: it is the real form of the supertrace-zero $4|4$ matrix Lie superalgebra preserving a Hermitian form with signature $(2,2)$ on the even block and positive signature on the odd block, modulo its central real line $\mathbb R\,iI_{4|4}$; for a block-diagonal matrix $A\oplus D$, the supertrace is $\operatorname{tr}A-\operatorname{tr}D$. Its even part is $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(4)_R$, with $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$; its odd generators are the Poincar\'e supercharges $Q,\bar Q$ and the special superconformal charges $S,\bar S$. The conformal generators include translations $P_\mu$, Lorentz transformations $M_{\mu\nu}$, dilations $D$, and special conformal transformations $K_\mu$. A superconformal primary is a state annihilated by all $K_\mu$ and all special superconformal charges; its descendants are obtained by applying $P_\mu$ and Poincar\'e supercharges. A unitary representation means that these generators act on a common invariant dense domain, the indicated adjoints are Hilbert adjoints, translations and radial Hamiltonian are self-adjoint, and the inner product is positive.

For the scalar-primary sector, use the selected $\mathcal N=1$ subalgebra and normalize its $U(1)_R$ generator $R$ so that the three adjoint chiral superfields have scalar charge $2/3$. Write $d_{\mathcal O}$ for the eigenvalue of the dilation generator on a scalar superconformal primary $|\mathcal O\rangle$ and $r_{\mathcal O}$ for its $R$ charge. The scalar unitarity bound in this convention is $d_{\mathcal O}\geq 3|r_{\mathcal O}|/2$; equality in the positive-charge branch is the chiral-primary shortening condition. The local conditional norm argument is given by the chiral-primary unitarity item on this page; no classification of all $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$ representations is asserted here.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

For the index sector require the closed odd operator $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ to be self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed composition equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply a simultaneous orthonormal energy/charge/parity eigenbasis for $\delta,J_1',\ldots,J_k'$ and $(-1)^F$, with real eigenlabels $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ and maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains. Here $\lambda\ge0$, the joint labels form a supplied countable set, and entire gap eigenspaces, including the protected kernel, may be infinite-dimensional. For every joint projection $P$, require $P D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP\psi=PT\psi$ for $T=Q,S,D_Q$ on $D(T)$. These reducing-domain conditions specify the actual spectral compatibility; common-domain commutators alone are insufficient. The grading preserves the joint subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains.

For $\beta>0$ and finite real or complex chemical potentials $\boldsymbol\mu$, define the weighted exponential first on the finite joint-eigenvector span by the eigenvalues $\exp(-\beta\lambda+\sum_a\mu_a j_a)$. Require its closure to be bounded trace class for every $\beta>0$ at the chosen $\boldsymbol\mu$. This is the meaning of the exponential in the index observable, not an unspecified product of unbounded operators. Every joint block then has finite dimension: its weight is nonzero and infinitely many equal singular values would violate trace class. Infinite total gap multiplicities are permitted through infinitely many joint blocks. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta,\boldsymbol\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H(S^3)}\left((-1)^F\exp\left[-\beta\delta+\sum_{a=1}^k\mu_aJ_a'\right]\right).$$

If the trace is not trace class, the same symbol may be used only for a specified formal series whose coefficients are defined; it does not denote a convergent partition function. The index is called protected against $\beta$-variation when the stated operator and trace hypotheses imply that positive-$\delta$ states cancel in the graded trace, as proved by the index-pair theorem on this page. A source's further claim of invariance under changing a coupling requires its own stated deformation hypotheses. A protected local operator means a named primary whose dimension is fixed by a specified shortening relation; the word alone asserts no deformation invariance.

For the quantum coupling family, use the source normalization

$$\tau=\frac{\theta}{2\pi}+\frac{4\pi i}{g^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0,$$

This is the physical component coupling family, not the formal Wilsonian coordinate $\tau_{\mathrm h}$ of the earlier zero-theta density bridge; no equality of the two parameter symbols is inferred. Here, on a closed oriented Euclidean four-manifold $X$ with an $SU(2)$ bundle, $k=-\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)\in\mathbb Z$ is the instanton number in the selected trace convention and $\theta$ weights its sectors by $e^{i\theta k}$. For the opposite, positive-ASD counting convention $k_{\mathrm A}=+\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)/(8\pi^2)$ on the same oriented manifold, one has $k_{\mathrm A}=-k$ by definition. The fixed physical gauge coefficient gives weight $q^k$ for a positive self-dual sector and $\bar q^{k_{\mathrm A}}$ for a positive anti-self-dual sector on the real coupling slice, where $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$. A local ADHM/Nekrasov pole orientation and weight identification is separate data; it is not obtained by equating these signed charge symbols. The corresponding source-reported $S$ and $T$ parameter maps are $S:\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$ and $T:\tau\mapsto\tau+1$. The global form and line-operator spectrum are part of the theory data, not determined by the Lie algebra alone. In the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ center-charge sector define $\mathcal C=\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ with charge $(e,m)$ and mutual-locality pairing

$$\langle(e,m),(e',m')\rangle=em'-me'\pmod 2.$$

An electric Wilson line is parallel transport traced in a representation of the global gauge group; a magnetic 't Hooft line is specified by a magnetic singularity around the support curve; a dyonic line carries both charges. Their center-charge classes are $(e,m)\in\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$. An allowed center-charge set is a subgroup $L\subseteq\mathcal C$ on which the displayed pairing vanishes; the three maximal such subgroups are the line-spectrum data for $SU(2)$, $SO(3)_+$, and $SO(3)_-$. The source-reported charge maps are $S:(e,m)\mapsto(m,-e)$ and $T:(e,m)\mapsto(e+m,m)$, so these transformations may change the global form. The 2007 and 2013 sources read for this item describe the quantum $S$-duality as a conjecture and refine it by global form and line data. This dated source status is recorded as such; this item does not assert an exhaustive literature-status review, an open-problem classification, or a proof of equivalence between the theories.

items.title: Positive-Supercharge Pair Cancellation in the Superconformal Index
items.design_state: Step 1 authored physics-theorem; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^{\bar 0}\oplus\mathcal H^{\bar 1}$ be a $\mathbb Z_2$-graded Hilbert space in a unitary representation of the selected four-dimensional superconformal algebra. Let $Q$ be the selected odd supercharge and $S=Q^\dagger$ its Hilbert adjoint. Assume a common invariant dense domain $D$ on which $Q^2=S^2=0$ and

$$\delta=2(SQ+QS)$$

is positive and extends to a self-adjoint operator. Assume that $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ is self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply an orthogonal countable direct sum of finite-dimensional reducing parity blocks $\mathcal H_b$, each contained in the common product domain, on which $\delta=\lambda_b I$ with $\lambda_b\ge0$. Repeated values of $\lambda_b$ are allowed, so total gap eigenspaces and the protected kernel may be infinite. Let $U$ be an even block-diagonal operator, on the maximal direct-sum domain containing the finite block span, whose finite restrictions commute with $Q,S$. Require the block operator $e^{-\beta\delta}U$ to extend to a trace-class operator for every $\beta>0$. This includes the original bounded-insertion finite-gap-eigenspace case. It also includes the full chemical-potential character in the earlier definition: its joint blocks reduce the charges, and their finite dimension follows from the nonzero exponential weights and trace class. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}\!\left((-1)^F e^{-\beta\delta}U\right),$$

where $(-1)^F$ acts as $+1$ on $\mathcal H^{\bar 0}$ and $-1$ on $\mathcal H^{\bar 1}$. Then

$$\mathcal I(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\ker\delta}\!\left((-1)^F U\right)$$

for every $\beta>0$. In particular, this trace is independent of $\beta$, and $\ker\delta=\ker Q\cap\ker S$. The conclusion applies to the superconformal index only when its Hilbert-space, operator-domain, spectral, commuting-charge, and trace hypotheses above hold; it makes no conclusion for continuous spectrum or a non-trace-class formal path integral.

items.title: Scalar Chiral-Primary Unitarity Bound
items.design_state: Step 1 authored physics-theorem; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a Hilbert-space representation of the selected $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal subalgebra, with positive inner product and common invariant domain on which the radial adjoint relations in the definition hold. Let $|\mathcal O\rangle\neq0$ be a scalar superconformal primary with dilation eigenvalue $d_{\mathcal O}$ and $U(1)_R$ eigenvalue $r_{\mathcal O}$. Then

$$d_{\mathcal O}\geq\frac32|r_{\mathcal O}|.$$

If $r_{\mathcal O}\geq0$, equality holds exactly when the selected chiral-branch supercharge $Q$ annihilates $|\mathcal O\rangle$. If $r_{\mathcal O}\leq0$, equality holds exactly when its conjugate $\bar Q$ annihilates $|\mathcal O\rangle$. This is a conditional algebraic statement about a state already present in the assumed unitary representation; it does not construct that representation or a continuum SCFT.

items.title: SU(2) and SO(3) Line-Spectrum Choices in the N=4 Duality Family
items.design_state: Step 1 authored example; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Use the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ center-charge group $\mathcal C=\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ with pairing $\langle(e,m),(e',m')\rangle=em'-me'\pmod2$. The source-reported line-spectrum subgroups associated with this gauge algebra are

$$L_{SU(2)}=\{(0,0),(1,0)\},\qquad L_{SO(3)_+}=\{(0,0),(0,1)\},\qquad L_{SO(3)_-}=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}.$$

Each is maximal among subgroups on which the pairing vanishes. Under the source-reported duality maps, $S:(e,m)\mapsto(m,-e)$ sends $L_{SU(2)}$ to $L_{SO(3)_+}$, while $T:(e,m)\mapsto(e+m,m)$ fixes $L_{SU(2)}$ and exchanges $L_{SO(3)_+}$ with $L_{SO(3)_-}$. The accompanying coupling maps are $S:\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$ and $T:\tau\mapsto\tau+1$. This verifies the finite line-charge permutation only; it does not prove that the quantum field theories related by these source-proposed maps are equivalent.

items.title: A Finite Boson–Fermion Pair in a Superconformal-Index Trace
items.design_state: Step 1 authored example; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C|b\rangle\oplus\mathbb C|f\rangle$ be a two-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal even state $|b\rangle$ and odd state $|f\rangle$. For a fixed $\lambda>0$, define an odd operator by $Q|b\rangle=\sqrt{\lambda/2}\,|f\rangle$ and $Q|f\rangle=0$, let $S=Q^\dagger$, and set $U=I$. With $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$, both states have eigenvalue $\lambda$, so $\ker\delta=\{0\}$. The graded trace from the SCFT-index definition is

$$\mathcal I(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}\left((-1)^F e^{-\beta\delta}\right)=e^{-\beta\lambda}-e^{-\beta\lambda}=0$$

for every $\beta>0$, equal to the trace on $\ker\delta$. This is a finite model of one supercharge pair only; it is not claimed to realize the full superconformal algebra or a four-dimensional gauge theory.

items.title: Conditional Dimension of the SU(2) Quadratic Chiral Primary
items.design_state: Step 1 authored example; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement: Use the selected N=4 SU(2) field data and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $Z$ be the complex scalar component of the first canonical adjoint chiral superfield; its engineering mass dimension is one and its selected N=1 $U(1)_R$ charge is $2/3$. Suppose a unitary quantum SCFT realization has a local operator algebra containing the nonzero scalar superconformal primary represented by the renormalized composite $\mathcal O=\operatorname{Tr}_2(Z^2)$, and suppose this state lies in the chiral branch. Then $\mathcal O$ has $R$ charge $4/3$ and scaling dimension exactly $2$. This is conditional shortening data for this specified operator state; it does not assert that the classical action constructs a continuum SCFT or that every scalar observable is protected.
